- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent low.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward in next 5–7 days — apply a “lag correction” by smoothing out the immediate drop.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model frequently overestimates near-term decline — adjust forecast downward by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — model tends to overpredict continuation of trend; apply a “reversion buffer” by adding 1–2% of recent 7-day average to forecast.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment shift.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–10) — apply a “warm-up correction” by reducing initial forecast by 3–8% if sentiment is negative or volatile.
